summaries.gardner: Trane has some Rule Breaker traits: it rides a clear trend (electrification and AI data-center cooling), has excellent management execution and the stock has beaten the S&P 500 over five years (+172% vs about +79% including dividends). But it is a century-old industrial in a mature industry, not a top dog in an emerging one, and the shares have lagged the market over the past year.
summaries.buffett: Trane fits much of Buffett's approach: an understandable business with a respected brand, recurring service revenue (about a third of sales), steady margin gains (operating margin 12.3% to 18.6%, 2020-2025), a ROIC near 27% and shareholder-friendly buybacks and dividends. The sticking point is price: at about 35 times trailing earnings there is little margin of safety.
summaries.munger: Munger would like the quality: a simple, essential product, rising margins, strong returns on capital and a well-regarded management team. Inverting, the main risks are a data-center spending bust and cyclical housing, which are survivable, but at around 30 times forward earnings the 'fair price for a great business' test is stretched.
summaries.lynch: Lynch would see Trane as a stalwart that has become a faster grower thanks to data centers, with a simple story: more buildings need more efficient cooling. Its P/E of about 35 against expected EPS growth around 15-17% gives a PEG near 2, above the level he liked, and Wall Street covers it heavily.
summaries.fisher: Trane scores well on Fisher's points: a sustained sales runway, management that keeps launching new products (EcoWise low-GWP line, quick-ship chillers, liquid cooling, BrainBox AI controls), widening margins, strong sales and service organisation and a respected culture. R&D is modest at about $348M (1.6% of sales), typical for HVAC.
summaries.graham: Trane fails most of Graham's defensive-investor tests on price: at about 35 times earnings and about 12 times book value, P/E times P/B exceeds 400 against Graham's 22.5 limit. It does pass on size, ten years of profits, dividends paid every year since 1910 and strong EPS growth.
summaries.thiel: Trane is not a Zero to One company: it has no tenfold technology lead and competes in an established oligopoly with Carrier, Daikin and Johnson Controls. It does score on distribution (direct sales and 7,500+ service technicians), durability and timing with the AI data-center build-out.
summaries.gerstner: Gerstner might appreciate Trane as a picks-and-shovels beneficiary of AI data-center build-outs, with bookings up 39% in Q2 2026 and a record $12.1B backlog, plus disciplined capital returns. Its revenue growth near 11% and a forward P/E around 30 are less compelling than the high-growth compounders he usually favours.
summaries.druckenmiller: The fundamental momentum is strong (record backlog, raised 2026 guidance, analysts' estimates rising), which Druckenmiller looks for, and data-center demand is a clear catalyst. But the share price has lagged the market over the past six and twelve months, and the stock is sensitive to any sign of a slowdown in AI capital spending.
summaries.smith: Trane comes close to a Terry Smith 'good company': high returns on capital (ROIC about 27%), steady growth, a third of revenue from recurring services and strong free-cash-flow conversion (2025 FCF $2.9B, 98% of net income). Its gross margin of 36% is below his ideal and the valuation (about 29 times free cash flow) tests 'don't overpay'.
summaries.greenblatt: Trane's return on capital is high (ROIC about 27%), but its earnings yield is low: 2025 operating income of $3.97B against an enterprise value near $105B is under 4%. It would rank well on quality and poorly on cheapness in the Magic Formula.
summaries.akre: Trane fits two legs of Akre's stool well: an extraordinary business with high returns and recurring service revenue, and capable, shareholder-minded management. The reinvestment leg is moderate, since much of free cash flow goes to dividends and buybacks rather than high-return reinvestment.
summaries.pabrai: Trane is not a Dhandho bet: it is a well-known, fully priced quality company rather than a simple business in a temporary distress at a deep discount. The risk of permanent loss is low, but the upside-to-downside asymmetry Pabrai demands is missing at about 35 times earnings.
summaries.wood: Trane sits at the edge of ARK's themes through energy efficiency, electrified heat pumps and AI data-center cooling, but it is not a disruptive-innovation platform company with falling cost curves. ARK-style investors would likely view it as an incumbent beneficiary rather than a disruptor.
summaries.ackman: Trane matches much of Ackman's checklist: a simple, predictable, free-cash-flow-generative business with a strong market position, pricing power and an investment-grade balance sheet. It is already well run, leaving little room for activist improvement, and the price is not at a discount.
summaries.sleep: Trane's scale lets it spread engineering and service costs and it reinvests in quick-ship capacity, but it does not systematically share scale savings with customers the way Nomad's favourites (Costco, Amazon) did. It is a quality compounder but not a classic scale-economics-shared model.
summaries.valentine: Valentine looked for huge markets and products solving painful problems; Trane addresses a large, essential need (cooling buildings and data centers) at the right time. It is, however, a mature incumbent rather than a young company creating a new market.
summaries.nash: Trane passes several of Nash's tests: it sells into the AI/energy infrastructure trend, is large, profitable, low on short interest and highly institutionally owned, and beats earnings expectations. It fails his instant-kill rules on operating margin (18.6% under 20%) and more debt than cash, its revenue growth is borderline at about 11%, and his DCF values it well below today's price.

momentum.evidence: TT fell about 5.6% from $491.42 (April 2026 month-end) to about $464 in October 2026 and rose only about 4% over twelve months, while SPY gained about 7% and 14% over the same periods.

g4.evidence: Long-serving CEO Dave Regnery has more than doubled EPS since 2021, and the shares are about 90% institutionally owned with 26 analysts covering it.

g6.evidence: At about 35 times trailing earnings, some analysts (Mizuho and RBC with Hold ratings) see limited upside, though the consensus is still Buy with a $529 average target.

simple.evidence: It makes and services heating, cooling and transport-refrigeration equipment, a business any careful generalist can understand.

b2.evidence: Revenue rose every year 2021-2025 and operating margin expanded every year from 12.3% (2020) to 18.6% (2025).

integrity.evidence: Management gives clear guidance it has repeatedly raised (2026 EPS guidance lifted from $14.65-$14.85 to $15.20-$15.30), returns cash via buybacks and dividends, and is named among Ethisphere's World's Most Ethical Companies for 2026.

b6.evidence: Acquisitions are small bolt-ons (about $720M deployed in 2025, plus Stellar Energy and BrainBox AI) focused on its core HVAC and controls business.

roic.evidence: ROIC is about 27% and ROE about 37%, with debt of $4.6B small relative to $3.97B of operating income.

fcf.evidence: 2025 free cash flow was $2,887.3M versus net earnings of $2,918.6M, about 99% conversion.

b10.evidence: Book equity grew from $6.1B (2022) to $8.6B (2025) despite $1.48B of 2025 buybacks, while market value rose far faster, to about $102B.

safety.evidence: A Nash-style DCF at a 12% discount rate gives about $197 a share versus a $465 price, so there is no margin of safety.

fairprice.evidence: A forward P/E near 30 for roughly 11% revenue and 15-17% EPS growth is full but arguably defensible for its quality and data-center exposure.

mu5.evidence: With essential products, a large installed base, about a third of revenue from services and low leverage, there are few ways the business itself could fail, though earnings can drop in a downturn.

reinvest.evidence: It reinvests at high returns in capacity, services and bolt-on deals, but capex is only about $383M a year and most free cash flow goes to dividends ($837M) and buybacks ($1.48B) in 2025.

ly2.evidence: A stalwart turned fast grower: more buildings and data centers need efficient cooling, and Trane is a leading supplier.

ly3.evidence: The trailing P/E of about 35 is roughly twice the expected 2026 adjusted EPS growth of about 17%.

runway.evidence: Electrification, refrigerant transitions, AI data centers and services growth give a multi-year runway, with a record $12.1B backlog and some orders scheduled for 2027 and beyond.

ly7.evidence: Diluted shares fell from 243.1M (2020) to 222.5M (Q2 2026) through buybacks, but there is no evidence of notable insider open-market buying.

ly8.evidence: It is a $100B-plus S&P 500 company covered by about 26 analysts.

fi2.evidence: It keeps launching new products such as EcoWise low-GWP equipment, quick-ship chillers, liquid cooling (Stellar Energy) and AI building controls (BrainBox AI).

fi3.evidence: R&D of $347.6M in 2025 supports margin gains and share wins in applied systems, with Americas applied bookings up 130% in Q2 2026.

fi4.evidence: Its direct sales and service network of over 7,500 technicians drives a services business of about one-third of revenue growing at a low-teens rate since 2020.

longterm.evidence: Management invests ahead of demand (quick-ship chiller capacity up more than 4x in two to three years) and set long-term sustainability targets such as the 2030 Gigaton Challenge.

gr1.evidence: 2025 revenue was $21.3B and its market value is about $102B.

ni10.evidence: It has been profitable every year in the last decade, including net earnings of $854.9M in pandemic-hit 2020 and $2,918.6M in 2025.

gr4.evidence: The company says it has paid annual dividends since 1910 and consecutive quarterly dividends since 1919.

eps10.evidence: Diluted EPS from continuing operations rose from $4.69 in 2019 to $13.14 in 2025, far more than a one-third gain.

gr6.evidence: The share price is about 35 times trailing earnings and well above 15 times average earnings.

gr7.evidence: P/E of about 35 times P/B of about 12 is more than 400, far above 22.5.

th1.evidence: Its chillers and HVAC systems are competitive but not ten times better than Carrier's, Daikin's or Johnson Controls'.

timing.evidence: AI data-center construction, electrification and refrigerant transitions are driving record demand, with Q2 2026 bookings up 39%.

th3.evidence: It is a long-established player in a large mature market rather than a startup that dominated a small niche first.

team.evidence: Regnery's team has grown EPS from $5.96 (2021) to $13.14 (2025) and expanded margins every year.

th5.evidence: A direct sales force, independent dealers and over 7,500 service technicians give it strong distribution.

durable.evidence: Buildings, food logistics and data centers will need heating and cooling for decades, and Trane's installed base and brands should hold, though cooling technology for data centers could shift.

th7.evidence: It moved early on sustainability and data-center chillers, but competitors see the same opportunities.

trend.evidence: It is a leading beneficiary of AI data-center build-outs and building electrification, with Americas applied bookings up 130% in Q2 2026.

dr1.evidence: Organic bookings growth accelerated from 11% in 2025 to 24% in Q1 and 37% in Q2 2026, and 2026 EPS guidance was raised twice.

dr2.evidence: The record $12.1B backlog points to faster revenue growth into 2027 (consensus about 9.8%), but much of this is already expected by the market.

dr4.evidence: Lower rates would help housing and construction, but residential HVAC is still weak and tariffs add about $200M of 2026 costs.

dr6.evidence: Conversion of the record backlog, Stellar Energy's data-center business and a residential recovery could drive results higher.

dr7.evidence: Quality and visibility are high, but valuation and data-center cyclicality argue against a very concentrated position.

gm.evidence: Gross margin of 36.2% (2025) is high for an industrial and rising, but not software-like.

fcfyield.evidence: The free-cash-flow yield is about 3.5%, modest but reasonable for a high-quality grower.

gb2.evidence: Operating income of $3.97B is under 4% of an enterprise value of about $105B.

pa2.evidence: The business is near record bookings and margins; only residential HVAC is in a temporary slump.

pa4.evidence: Permanent loss of capital is unlikely given its essential products, low leverage and strong cash flow, even if the multiple could compress.

wo1.evidence: It supplies cooling for AI data centers and energy-efficiency technology, but is not itself an AI or energy-storage technology leader.

wo2.evidence: HVAC product costs are not falling quickly with volume; margin gains came from pricing and mix.

wo3.evidence: It combines equipment, AI-based building controls (BrainBox AI) and data-center liquid cooling, but these are adjacent HVAC capabilities rather than separate platforms.

wo4.evidence: Its addressable market grows high-single to low-double digits a year, not many times over in five years.

ac3.evidence: It passes on most cost inflation through price, but is exposed to metal costs, tariffs (about $200M in 2026) and interest-rate-sensitive construction and housing.

ns1.evidence: Trane has used scale to raise margins rather than to cut prices for customers.

ns4.evidence: Its position in data-center cooling and services is likely stronger in a decade, but Asian rivals and new cooling technologies could erode share.

va2.evidence: Keeping buildings, food and data centers at the right temperature efficiently is a large and costly problem for owners.

tn1.evidence: It sells into the AI and energy infrastructure trend, but it is a century-old HVAC business benefiting from the trend rather than one built for it.

tn2.evidence: The market increasingly sees it as an AI data-center play, though it remains mostly a commercial and residential HVAC company, so the gap is modest.

tn3.evidence: It is a large-cap, Irish-domiciled, US-centred industrial, not in any of the zones to avoid.

tn4.evidence: Revenue has grown every year since 2020 and it is solidly profitable; the one miss is that debt ($4.6B) exceeds cash ($1.3B).

tn5.evidence: Free cash flow has been positive, but debt has exceeded cash in every recent quarter (June 2026: $4.6B debt vs $1.3B cash).

tn6.evidence: Revenue grew 7.5% in 2025 but is guided to about 11.5% in 2026.

tn7.evidence: About 11% expected 2026 revenue growth plus a free-cash-flow margin near 14-16% totals under 30.

tn8.evidence: In 2025 revenue grew 7.5% while operating income grew 13.4%, so costs grew more slowly than revenue.

tn9.evidence: It fails two instant kills: more debt ($4.6B) than cash ($1.3B) and an operating margin of 18.6% (2025) below 20%.

tn10.evidence: No major regulatory threat to the business, though it carries legacy asbestos liabilities (handled through its Aldrich and Murray subsidiaries) and faces refrigerant rule changes.

tn11.evidence: Trane provides heating, cooling and refrigeration systems that help building owners, data centers and fleets keep spaces and cargo at the right temperature efficiently, and charges for equipment plus service contracts and parts.

tn13.evidence: Score about 90: cash vs debt 0, revenue growth 5, operating margin 5, short interest 10 (1.7%), institutional ownership 10 (90%), revenue faster than expenses 10, 5-year return vs S&P 10 (+172% vs +79%), moat 5, CEO 5, pricing power 5, secular trend 10, culture and mission 10, talent 5.

tn14.evidence: Revenue grew and operating margin expanded every year 2021-2025, but free cash flow fell in 2021 and 2022 and debt exceeded cash every year.

tn15.evidence: Interest coverage is about 17.5x and the current ratio 1.25 with liabilities 1.5x equity, but assets excluding goodwill ($15.0B) are only 1.17x liabilities ($12.8B).

tn18.evidence: Regnery has a strong execution record since July 2021, but has been CEO only about five years, is not a founder and there is no record of large open-market share purchases.

tn20.evidence: It beat estimates in Q1 2026 (adjusted EPS $2.63 vs $2.53 consensus) and Q2 2026 ($4.31 vs $4.20-$4.25 guidance), raising full-year guidance each time.

tn21.evidence: No red flags: a single long-serving CEO, small bolt-on deals, rising margins, no accounting concerns and no auditor change found.

tn22.evidence: It has $21B of revenue, strong profits and shrinking share count, the opposite of a hype stock.

tn24.evidence: A reverse DCF at today's $465 price implies sustained growth well above the roughly 10% revenue growth it has delivered over three years.

tn25.evidence: Using 10.1% average growth, a 13.3% FCF margin, 4% terminal growth and a 12% discount rate gives about $197 a share, far below $465.

tn26.evidence: A forward P/E of about 30 versus expected EPS growth of about 17% gives a PEG near 1.8 (StockAnalysis shows 1.91), above 1.
